entities.summary: Joseph Michael Acabá is an American educator, hydrogeologist, and NASA astronaut. In May 2004, he became the first person of Puerto Rican ancestry to be named as a NASA astronaut candidate, when he was selected as a member of NASA Astronaut Training Group 19. He completed his training on February 10, 2006, and was assigned to STS-119, which flew from March 15 to 28, 2009, to deliver the final set of solar arrays to the International Space Station. He is the first person of Caribbean and Puerto Rican origin, and the twelfth of fifteen people of Ibero-american heritage to have flown to space as a NASA astronaut.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the first person of Caribbean and Puerto Rican origin to fly to space, Joseph M. Acaba's achievement paved the way for greater diversity in NASA's astronaut corps and inspired a new generation of scientists and explorers from underrepresented backgrounds.
